verses.text: After Saul died, David came back from defeating the Amalekites and stayed two days in Ziklag.
On the third day a man came from Saul's camp, with his clothes torn and dust on his head. When he came to David, he bowed down to the ground to show respect.
David asked him, "Where have you come from?" He said, "I have escaped from the camp of Israel."
David said, "What happened? Please tell me." He answered, "The army ran away from the battle, and many of the people fell and died. Saul and his son Jonathan are dead too."
David asked the young man who brought the news, "How do you know that Saul and his son Jonathan are dead?"
The young man said, "I happened to be on Mount Gilboa, and I saw Saul leaning on his spear. The chariots and horsemen were closing in on him.
He looked behind him, saw me, and called to me. I answered, 'Here I am.'
He asked me, 'Who are you?' I told him, 'I am an Amalekite.'
Then he said to me, 'Please stand over me and kill me. I am in terrible pain, but I am still alive.'
So I stood over him and killed him, because I knew he could not live after he had fallen. Then I took the crown from his head and the band from his arm, and I have brought them here to you, my lord."
Then David grabbed his own clothes and tore them, and all the men with him did the same.
They mourned and cried and went without food until evening for Saul and his son Jonathan, for the LORD's people, and for the nation of Israel, because they had been killed by the sword.
David asked the young man who brought the news, "Where are you from?" He answered, "I am the son of a foreigner, an Amalekite."
David said to him, "Why were you not afraid to lift your hand to kill the LORD's chosen king?"
Then David called one of his young men and said, "Go and strike him down!" So he struck him, and he died.
David said to him, "Your blood is on your own head. Your own mouth spoke against you when you said, 'I killed the LORD's chosen king.'"
Then David sang this sad song about Saul and his son Jonathan.
He ordered that the people of Judah be taught this song, called the Song of the Bow. It is written in the Book of Jashar:
"Israel, your glory lies dead on your hills! How the mighty heroes have fallen!
Do not tell it in Gath. Do not announce it in the streets of Ashkelon, or the daughters of the Philistines will be glad, and the daughters of those outsiders will celebrate.

Mountains of Gilboa, let no dew or rain fall on you, and let no fields grow crops for offerings. For there the shield of the mighty was made dirty and thrown away. The shield of Saul was no longer rubbed with oil.
Jonathan's bow never turned back from the blood of the dead and the bodies of the strong. Saul's sword never came back empty.
Saul and Jonathan were loved and kind in their lives, and in their death they were not separated. They were faster than eagles and stronger than lions.
Daughters of Israel, cry for Saul. He dressed you in fine red clothes and put gold jewellery on your clothes.
How the mighty heroes have fallen in the middle of the battle! Jonathan lies dead on your hills.
I am heartbroken for you, my brother Jonathan. You were so dear to me. Your love for me was wonderful, greater than the love of women.
How the mighty heroes have fallen, and their weapons of war are destroyed!"
